title: `TypedArray<>` does not export C# bindings correctly if the type is `int64_t` or `uint64_t`
body:
### Tested versions

v4.2.1.stable.mono.official [b09f793f5]
v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8]
v4.5.1.stable.mono.official [f62fdbde1]

### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable.mono (f62fdbde1) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8108) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz (20 threads) - 31.85 GiB memory

### Issue description

I first noticed this bug when I had to use `PhysicsTestMotionParameters3D::set_exclude_objects`, which accepts what should be an array of `ObjectID`. This is not a variant type, so the current C++ implementation exports it as `TypedArray<uint64_t>`.

The problem arises when the C# version of the API is created. The property (and its getter/setter) are incorrectly interpreted as `Array<int>` rather than `Array<ulong>`, which is particularly egregious when it comes to `ObjectID`.

Still, this is not exactly urgent even if it does make that method effectively unusable. The `exclude_bodies` property which accepts `Array<Rid>` is the better choice *basically* every time. Regardless, I've implemented a temporary stopgap in my fork by changing it to a variant `Array`. I'm not aware of any cleaner solutions, but if there is one I can implement until an official fix is released, do let me know.

Thank you.
